title: Model SafeMode: catalog-recommended quant profiles + calibration runbook
creator: Elena Rodriguez
description:
Goal: Produce a per-model "SafeMode" recommendation that ships in the model catalog alongside each model entry. SafeMode provides a small portfolio of recommended quantization configurations (FP8-likely, INT8-conservative) plus a prescriptive calibration and validation runbook. The deliverable will include: (1) a deterministic selection heuristic for assigning a recommended default and a conservative fallback for each catalog model, (2) an automated calibration harness for nightly shadow runs, (3) accuracy regression thresholds and rollback criteria, and (4) documentation and console UI messaging for customers to understand recommended trade-offs.

Motivation: Customers frequently ask for a single, safe quantization choice per model that balances cost and accuracy risk. Current catalog lacks a unified contract for defaults and the runbook ops teams need to validate changes. This ticket creates the product + engineering contract to reduce surprise regressions when quantization is applied in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope: Applies to all models in the catalog initially for which we have transformer-based FP16 baselines. Excludes experimental sparse or exotic architectures in the rollout phase. The deliverable will be stored in the catalog metadata (recommended_profiles, fallback_chain, expected_accuracy_delta_percent) and surfaced in the Console.

Non-goals: Building new quant kernels, building a new calibration tool from scratch (we will extend existing calibrator harness), or changing runtime fallback mechanisms beyond configuration parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Each catalog model entry has a SafeMode record consisting of: recommended_profile (string), fallback_profile (string), expected_accuracy_delta (string percent), and calibration_artifact_link (url)
Automated nightly shadow calibration runs complete for a seeded set of 50 representative models with metrics captured in the calibration dashboard
Regression guardrail defined: any >1.5% absolute drop on core eval suite triggers an automated rollback and alert to the platform SRE/ML owners
Console shows a concise SafeMode summary and a link to the calibration runbook for each model
Documentation published: runbook, validation checklist, and operator playbook for rolling a new recommended_profile
steps: Design the SafeMode metadata schema and storage fields in catalog (product + infra sync)
Create the selection heuristic: dataset fingerprint -> profile suggestion; include confidence score and decision rationale
Integrate calibration harness to run shadow quantized inference against nightly eval sets and store artifacts
Define regression detection rules, alerting, and automatic rollback hooks
Implement Console display and link to documentation
Run staged rollout: internal-only -> partner beta -> general availability
Produce operator runbook and run a DR exercise with SRE on rollback scenario
test_plan: Unit tests for SafeMode metadata serialization and migrations
End-to-end test: pick 5 models, apply recommended_profile in shadow mode, compare token-level and BLEU/QA metrics to FP16 baseline
Stress test: run calibration harness at catalog-scale (50 models) overnight and validate resource use and time-to-completion
False-positive check: seed intentional calibration noise to validate alert thresholds and rollback behavior
Canary rollout: enable recommended_profile for 1% traffic on Dedicated and monitor latency/accuracy telemetry for 72 hours
decisions: Calibration harness will run in shadow mode by default; only after passing GA criteria will profiles be enabled for live traffic
Regression threshold set to 1.5% absolute accuracy drop for core eval suite; lower-tier models use relative thresholds specified in metadata
FP8 will be suggested only when model numeric sensitivity score < 0.12 and dataset fingerprint similarity > 0.85
Store SafeMode artifacts as immutable calibration bundles referenced by catalog entry (S3 path + SHA)
Security: calibration artifacts encrypted with customer-facing KMS keys for Private deployments

notes: Edge cases: small fine-tuned models trained on narrow domains often show brittle FP8 behavior; SafeMode will default them to INT8-conservative profile
